review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped uses in Mathlib. The only simp rules are fdifferential_apply, hfdifferential_apply and fdifferential_comp. Nothing was run, so the competition between rules is a prediction from simp's inside-out rewriting and not an observed failure. I found no evidence of loops. I did not recommend @[simp] for smul_def, because downstream code uses it only through explicit rw. I did not recommend it for Derivation.evalAt_apply either. It is already used by name in other files, and it is a plain rfl lemma.

findings.excerpt:
theorem fdifferential_comp (g : C^∞⟮I', M'; I'', M''⟯) (f : C^∞⟮I, M; I', M'⟯) (x : M) :
    𝒅 (g.comp f) x = (𝒅 g (f x)).comp (𝒅 f x) :=
findings.problem: This rule is @[simp] and competes with the simp lemma fdifferential_apply. Simp rewrites subterms first. In `𝒅 (g.comp f) x v h` it should therefore rewrite the inner `𝒅 (g.comp f) x` into a composite of linear maps before fdifferential_apply can match the whole application. After LinearMap.comp_apply and fdifferential_apply, the result is `v ((h.comp g).comp f)`. The direct route gives `v (h.comp (g.comp f))`. The file has no simp lemma for associativity of ContMDiffMap.comp. The only simp lemma I found in ContMDiffMap.lean is comp_apply, so the two routes may not converge. The same input can then reach different normal forms, depending on whether it is applied to a vector. The rule also expands a single differential into a composite in contexts where nobody asked for that.
findings.proposed_change: Remove @[simp] from fdifferential_comp and let fdifferential_apply be the only simp rule for evaluated differentials. Callers who want the chain rule can use it explicitly, as LeftInvariantDerivation.lean already does with `rw [..., fdifferential_comp, ...]`. If it is kept as simp, add a simp lemma for associativity of ContMDiffMap.comp so both routes reach one normal form.
findings.benefit: Evaluated differentials normalize in a way that doesn't depend on rewrite order, and simp no longer splits `𝒅 (g.comp f) x` into a composite unprompted. Existing explicit `rw` uses are unaffected.
